what-a-reverse-proxy-does.r: A company exposed three apps on three public ports and three certificates. A single reverse proxy gave them one address, one certificate and one place to add logging and limits.
what-a-reverse-proxy-does.x: Put one well-run front door in front of many services, and keep the apps behind it private. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

nginx-configuration-servers-and-location.r: An engineer added a regex location for images and suddenly the API stopped working. A regex location beat the prefix location for /api/, and the request went to the wrong place.
nginx-configuration-servers-and-location.x: Know the match order and always test the config before reload. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

proxying-to-upstreams-headers-and-buffer.r: A login page worked on the intranet but redirected users to http://localhost:3000 behind the proxy. The application built redirect URLs from the Host header it received, and the proxy had not passed the original host.
proxying-to-upstreams-headers-and-buffer.x: The proxy must tell the app what the user saw, and only the proxy should be allowed to say it. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

tls-termination-http2-and-certificates.r: A certificate expired at 03:00 on a Sunday because the renewal job had failed silently for two months. Browsers showed a full-page warning and traffic fell to zero.
tls-termination-http2-and-certificates.x: Automate renewal and alert well before expiry; a certificate that depends on a person is an outage waiting.

load-balancing-algorithms-and-health-che.r: One of four backends hung but still accepted connections. Round robin kept sending it a quarter of the requests, and one in four users saw timeouts for an hour.
load-balancing-algorithms-and-health-che.x: A load balancer is only as good as its health check. Check what users need, not just that the port is open.

timeouts-retries-keepalive-and-limits.r: A report endpoint took 70 seconds. The proxy read timeout was 60, so users got a 504 even though the app finished correctly and spent the effort. Raising one timeout fixed it, but the real fix was an asynchronous job.
timeouts-retries-keepalive-and-limits.x: Timeouts should shrink as you go up the stack: callers wait longer than the services they call. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

caching-compression-and-static-files.r: A page showing the logged-in user's name was cached by the proxy. For ten minutes everyone saw the first user's name. The cache key had ignored the cookie.
caching-compression-and-static-files.x: Cache what is the same for everyone, and be explicit about what is not. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

rate-limiting-and-protecting-backends.r: A mobile app bug retried failed requests in a tight loop. Without limits it sent 5,000 requests a second from a few thousand devices and took down the API. A per-client limit would have contained it.
rate-limiting-and-protecting-backends.x: Limit by who is calling, not just by total volume, and fail with a clear 429. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

haproxy-frontends-backends-and-acls.r: A team needed to route and rate-limit at wire speed with live state to inspect. HAProxy's stats page and runtime socket let them drain a server and see queue depth without a restart.
haproxy-frontends-backends-and-acls.x: HAProxy shines when you need to see and change live traffic state safely. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

envoy-traefik-and-dynamic-proxies.r: A team with hundreds of containers that came and went could not reload nginx fast enough. Traefik watched the container engine and updated routes automatically.
envoy-traefik-and-dynamic-proxies.x: In a dynamic environment, let the platform tell the proxy what exists instead of editing files. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

zero-downtime-reloads-and-blue-green-at-.r: A config change was applied with a restart in business hours. Every open connection dropped, and a thousand uploads failed. A reload, or a canary, would have kept them.
zero-downtime-reloads-and-blue-green-at-.x: Never restart a proxy to change config; reload it, and send traffic gradually to new versions. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.

debugging-502-504-and-proxy-problems.r: After a backend IP changed, nginx kept sending to the old address for hours because it had resolved the name only at startup. Every request returned 502 until someone reloaded.
debugging-502-504-and-proxy-problems.x: Read the proxy's own log first. It usually says which side failed and why. Check the facts first, change one thing at a time, and write down what you learned.
